about: pass 2 arrows (C2a-02), from c2_arrow_evidence-p2a.txt and -p2b.txt; every count, transition and sampled room copied from those files; mechanisms and fail clauses were written in notes-C2.md before the counts
sample_rule: sampled_against: rooms carrying both elements outside the twenty pass 1 story rooms, drawn by random.Random(20261014) in c2_arrow_evidence.py; holds when the connection statement holds in that room, fails when it does not

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first act of upkeep or defence comes before the first help given, asked for or traded with another room
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the repair and defence themes against the exchange themes (all of Reciprocity); 106 transitions in 44 rooms where a call for help or an offer of help answers a report of erosion. Disconfirming: help traded only before any upkeep.
arrows.mechanism: A room keeping its work under strain runs short of hands and turns to other rooms for help, and other rooms send it.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, help is given, asked for or traded only before any upkeep or defence, or a room under strain never asks for or receives help.
arrows.bound: Where a room helps a neighbour before it has a work of its own to keep, or comes to the canvas as another room's helper, exchange comes first.
arrows.counterexample_response: 69 of 240 rooms give or ask for help before their first upkeep. Alternatives considered: a coding artefact (help is coded late), or a second path where help is the room's first relation to the canvas. The pass 1 story rooms show the second path (MiamiHurricanes keeps a coalition's work; xenoblade_chronicles receives help from r/Bulgaria). Response: a scope condition in the bound; the arrow is fair, not strong.
arrows.gloss: short of hands, a room turns to other rooms

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first border talk, truce or deal comes before the first help given, asked for or traded with another room
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the border and truce themes against the exchange themes; 108 transitions in 44 rooms where help answers a border settled or a deal offered. Disconfirming: help traded only before any border talk.
arrows.mechanism: Talk over a border opens a channel through which the two rooms then trade help: room for upkeep, pixels for protection.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, help is traded only before any border talk, or settled borders are never followed by help between the two rooms.
arrows.bound: Thin: 0.645 against a null 95th percentile of 0.636, one of twelve order tests at pass 2. Where a room's first relation to a neighbour is help, help comes first.
arrows.counterexample_response: 76 of 214 rooms trade help before any border talk. Response: uncertainty; the arrow is kept thin and theorised beside its stronger sibling A13.
arrows.gloss: a settled border opens a channel for help

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first call to the canvas comes before the room's first call or act against another room's work
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the calling themes against the attack themes (all of Repertoire of contention), read in the room whose threads hold them (the visitor rule); 34 transitions in 19 rooms where an attack call answers a call to place. Disconfirming: attack calls only before any call to place.
arrows.mechanism: A call brings members to the canvas, and some of them turn its hands against a rival's work instead of, or before, building the room's own.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, calls to attack come only before any call to place, or calls to place are never followed by a call or act against another room's work.
arrows.bound: Where a room's first canvas act is an attack (edmontonoilers, canucks, anarcho_capitalism among the pass 1 story rooms), the attack call is the first call.
arrows.counterexample_response: 36 of 129 rooms call an attack before any call to place. Alternatives considered: the call to place is coded only once it names the room's own mark, so attack-first rooms are rooms with no mark yet. The pass 1 readings support this (canucks: 'Since we aren't doing our own'). Response: a scope condition in the bound.
arrows.gloss: a call's hands can turn on a rival

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the room's first call or act against another room's work comes before its first sparing, refusal, apology or reining in
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the attack themes against the restraint themes (all of Live and let live); 127 transitions in 52 rooms where a refusal answers an attack call within minutes. Disconfirming: restraint only before any attack call.
arrows.mechanism: A call to attack another room's work is answered inside the room: members refuse it, rein in their attackers or apologise to the target.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, sparing and restraint come only before any attack call, or attack calls draw no refusal.
arrows.bound: Partly constitutive: reining in the room's own attackers needs an attack to rein in. Where sparing is tacit and comes first (touhou at h3.6, calgaryflames at h9.9), restraint precedes any attack call.
arrows.counterexample_response: 22 of 104 rooms spare before any attack call; two sampled rooms (touhou, calgaryflames) run this way. Alternatives considered: the arrow as pure definition. Against it, 127 transitions show a refusal by another member answering a specific attack call, which a definition would not order. Response: kept strong, with the tacit-sparing path as a scope condition.
arrows.gloss: an attack call is refused inside the room

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the room's first call or act against another room's work comes before its first border talk, truce or deal
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the attack themes against the border and truce themes; 73 transitions in 35 rooms where a truce or deal is invoked in reply to an attack call. Disconfirming: border talk only before any attack call.
arrows.mechanism: A call to attack is met by the room's relations with its neighbours: members invoke a truce, or propose a deal instead.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, border talk comes only before any attack call, or attack calls are never answered with talk.
arrows.bound: Early side only: on the late side border talk comes first (0 of 4 hold), since late rooms meet neighbours before any attack.
arrows.counterexample_response: 77 of 172 rooms talk borders before any attack call; all four late rooms do. strangerthings (talk at h33.0, attack at h62.2) is one. Response: a scope condition (the late side) and fair strength.
arrows.gloss: an attack call is met with a truce

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the room's first call or act against another room's work comes before the first taunt, chant, claim of victory or salute with a rival
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the attack themes against the rivalry themes (all of Rivalry); 50 transitions in 14 rooms where a taunt answers an attack call. Disconfirming: rivalry talk only before any attack.
arrows.mechanism: An attack makes the rival a named party, and the contest is carried on in talk: taunts, chants, claims of victory, a salute after the fight.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, rivalry talk comes only before any attack, or an attack is never followed by talk with or about the rival.
arrows.bound: Early side only: no late-side room carries both.
arrows.counterexample_response: 12 of 68 rooms taunt before any attack, among them rooms whose rivalry comes from outside the canvas. Response: uncertainty; the arrow cannot be tested on the late side, so it is fair, not strong.
arrows.gloss: an attack is carried on in taunts

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first act of upkeep or defence comes before the first alliance, shared chat, joint mark or request to host
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the repair and defence themes against the coalition themes (all of Meta-organization); 52 transitions in 28 rooms where an alliance is proposed in reply to a call to defend. Disconfirming: coalitions only before any upkeep.
arrows.mechanism: A room keeping its work against attack joins other rooms whose works face the same threat, and they defend each other's works together.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, coalitions come only before any upkeep or defence, or a room under attack never joins with another.
arrows.bound: Late side: 2 of 7 hold; late rooms join a coalition or ask a host first, entering the canvas through other rooms (bretagne, MiamiHurricanes, yuyuyu). Thin: one of twelve order tests at pass 2.
arrows.counterexample_response: 51 of 157 rooms join a coalition before any upkeep; the late side mostly does. Response: a scope condition (the late side) and thin strength.
arrows.gloss: under attack, works defend each other
